# 🧰 The environment track

[← The Road](../README.md) · [📊 Grading](../GRADING.md) · [📌 Standing rules](../STANDING-RULES.md)

**One 30-minute test every week, taken on Day 5. Scored out of 10, reported separately from your day scores.**

---

## Why this track exists

Look at what you have actually been doing since 22 July:

- You have run `git add`, `git commit` and `git push` **every single day for two weeks**.
- You have been told to open **DevTools** before every commit — it is a standing rule.
- You are using a **terminal** and an **editor** for hours a day.

**And not one of those has ever been taught to you.** In the original plan, Git is Week 10 and DevTools is Week 11 — more than two months away. You have been using tools you were never shown, which is exactly how people end up with five years of experience and a `git push --force` habit that costs their team a day of work.

For someone doing an internship rather than a hobby course, that ordering is wrong. So this track runs **alongside** the CSS and JavaScript weeks instead of waiting its turn.

> **The rule of this track: everything in it is a tool you are already using.** Nothing here is new work — it is being asked to actually know the things in your hands.

---

## 📅 The schedule

| Week | Test | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [02](week-02/) | **Terminal, files & Git basics** | paths, `cd`/`ls`/`mv`, what a commit *is*, staging vs committing, reading `git status` and `git log` |
| 03 | **DevTools** | Elements, computed styles, strike-throughs, the box-model panel, device toolbar, Network |
| 04 | **Git for real** | branches, merges, `.gitignore`, what to do when a push is rejected, undoing things safely |
| 05 | **The editor & the shell** | multi-cursor, find-in-project, integrated terminal, pipes, `grep` |
| 06+ | announced in the week review | |

## 📋 How it is scored

Out of 10, same shape as the daily tests: recall, predict, spot-the-bug, defend.

- Reported in [SCOREBOARD.md](../SCOREBOARD.md) in its own column.
- **Below 6 twice in a row → the week repeats.** One bad week is a bad week; two is a gap.
- Closed book, **30 minutes**, no AI. Same honesty rules as the daily test.

## 🎯 What "knowing your tools" is worth

The difference between a developer who is fast and one who is slow is almost never typing speed or how much syntax they have memorised. It is this:

- Finding the one line that matters in a 4,000-line file in **three seconds** instead of three minutes.
- Seeing *why* a style did not apply instead of guessing and re-running.
- Undoing a mistake **calmly**, because you know exactly what `git reset` does and does not touch.

None of that is glamorous, none of it appears in a tutorial, and it compounds every single day for the rest of your career.
